To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proximal tubular reabsorption of phosphate is mediated by Na‐coupled cotransporters, and that mutations in the genes that encode these transporters result in a variety of inherited disorders of renal phosphate reabsorption.
the renal proximal tubule reabsorbs approximately 90% of filtered phosphate, and that this reabsorption is mediated by Na 1 -dependent phosphate cotransporters.
the renal Na 1 -P i cotransporter gene (NPT2) is expressed in the kidney in a segment‐ and species‐specific manner and is regulated at the level of gene transcription and/or mRNA stability.

the proximal tubular cell possesses a variety of transport systems that mediate the net reabsorption of filtered Pi.
